name: Light Tyrian Blue
lede: Light Tyrian Blue is a paler, greyer step off [[tyrian-blue|Tyrian Blue]], the blue sibling of Tyrian purple, the ancient shellfish dye.

sections.title: A modifier on the shellfish dye's blue
sections.body:
The name is built by grammar: "light" over the parent [[tyrian-blue|Tyrian Blue]], whose best-known story is a religious one tied to Tyrian purple [1]. Ridgway's 1912 atlas plates this lighter, greyer step at plate XXXIV, hue 47'', and ISCC-NBS separately filed it in 1955 as block 186 [1]. Measured, it is only a little lighter than its parent and far less saturated (chroma 16 against 17, close; lightness 53 against 51), reading as a soft slate blue [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[tyrian-blue|Tyrian Blue]] itself, 2.6 units away and almost the same, with [[slate]] close behind, also 2.6 and almost the same [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this slate blue in 290 of 23,781 paintings (1.22 percent, as photographed), more common than 66 percent of the named colors we track [2]. It most often plays a hidden color, in 47 percent of its strongest matches, and peaks in paintings from the 1900s [2]. The earliest dated match runs to 1405, by Spinello Aretino, 507 years before Ridgway's 1912 record; a floor, not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].
